advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the outbound-preservation test write an EDIT/STATUS whose payload actually names creation_channel (e.g. attempts to set it to a different value) and assert genesis 'python' survives.
evidence: rebar.edit_ticket(tid, description='synced from jira', ...) and rebar.claim(tid, assignee='me', ...) — neither writes a creation_channel field

Contrast: tests/interfaces/facades/test_creation_channel.py:218-229 injects data.fields creation_channel='cli' into an EDIT and asserts it is skipped — that test actually exercises _IMMUTABLE_EDIT_FIELDS; this one does not.
advisory.finding: test_outbound_sync_edit_preserves_creation_channel claims to guard AC2 (later mutation never rewrites genesis creation_channel) but the edit_ticket/claim it issues never carries a creation_channel field in the EDIT payload, so the final assertion passes even if the _IMMUTABLE_EDIT_FIELDS guard were removed. It does not exercise the immutability seam the way the existing test_immutable_edit_cannot_replace_genesis_creation_channel does (which injects creation_channel into the EDIT fields).
scenarios: The immutable-field guard for creation_channel is removed/weakened; this test still passes because no EDIT ever names creation_channel.
advisory.suggested_fix: Construct or issue a writeback EDIT that includes creation_channel in its fields (as the immutable-edit facade test does) so the assertion fails if the guard is dropped.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an import test whose source NDJSON record carries a non-python, non-import creation_channel and assert the imported local ticket still reports 'import'.
evidence: test_import_records_import_channel comment: '# The source ticket carries a python channel; export includes it.' then 'assert imported["creation_channel"] == "import"'
src/rebar/_io/_provenance.py:34: '"_creation_channel": "import",' (static literal — the documented 'independent of the exported source record's own channel' behavior)

import_ndjson.py:229 feeds create_kwargs(rec) to create_ticket, and import_tickets accepts raw NDJSON, so a record carrying creation_channel='jira' could be constructed to prove independence — but no test does this.
dropped.finding: The import 'independence' contract — the fresh local ticket records creation_channel='import' regardless of the channel the exported source record carried — is only tested against a source whose channel is 'python'. Since create_kwargs pins a static literal 'import', a regression that instead copies record.get('creation_channel') would still pass this test (python source vs import are trivially distinct only because the literal is hardcoded).
scenarios: A future refactor makes create_kwargs read record.get('creation_channel') as a fallback; a source ticket exported with a non-import channel would then be copied instead of pinned to 'import'.
dropped.suggested_fix: Feed rebar.import_tickets a hand-built record dict with e.g. creation_channel='jira' (or mutate the exported line) and assert the imported ticket's creation_channel == 'import' and source_* preserves the origin.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test where a CREATE records a real channel (e.g. 'cli') AND carries the jira- id + reconciler/reconciler signature, asserting the reduced channel stays the recorded value with no creation_channel_inferred marker.
evidence: _write_legacy_create docstring: 'Build a channel-less legacy CREATE' — data never contains creation_channel
docs/event-schema.md diff: 'A post-feature CREATE that recorded a real channel is never touched.' — asserted in docs but not covered by a test
dropped.finding: The 'a post-feature CREATE that recorded a real channel is never touched by the legacy inference' contract has no regression test: the reducer guards inference on `if data.get('creation_channel') is None`, but _write_legacy_create always omits creation_channel, so no test writes a CREATE with BOTH a recorded channel AND the legacy-Jira signature (jira- id + reconciler author + reconciler env_id).
scenarios: The guard is changed (e.g. to key off state instead of raw data, or dropped); a CREATE that recorded python/cli/mcp but happens to bear a jira- id + reconciler/reconciler envelope would be overwritten to inferred 'jira' with no test catching it.
dropped.suggested_fix: Extend _write_legacy_create (or add a variant) to accept an optional recorded creation_channel, then assert that with channel='cli' + full jira signature the state keeps 'cli' and has no creation_channel_inferred.
